Michael Imeretinsky (1900–1975) was a British military officer of Georgian royal lineage, descended from the Bagrationi dynasty and the kings of the western Georgian kingdom of Imereti. Born in Saint Petersburg to Prince George Imeretinsky and Lidya Klimova, he graduated from Lancing College in the United Kingdom and joined the Royal Flying Corps as a sub-lieutenant in 1918. He served in both World War I and World War II, eventually commanding a squadron in the Royal Air Force Volunteer Reserve, and was awarded the Air Force Cross. After retiring from the military, he lived in the United Kingdom and France, where he pursued agriculture and horticulture, and became a prominent member of the Soil Association.

Imeretinsky died in Nice in 1975 at the age of 75, reportedly the last direct male descendant of the kings of Imereti. He married Margaret Stella Wright in 1925, and they had three daughters: Tamara, Natalia, and Nadezhda. The biography notes his aristocratic heritage and his later life as a horticulturist in France, alongside the military service that earned him the Air Force Cross.
